correctness.rationale: Fresh exact enumeration by GF(2) row reduction and outdegree filtering recovered 600 balanced states among 8192 parity-admissible vectors. The rank-11 incidence constraints imply 2048 full characters per restricted character up to a fixed sign. The reduced integer Walsh transform gave 3553 nonzero, 4639 zero and minimum nonzero magnitude 4; the full counts are 7276544 and 9500672. Reversal forces 8388608 odd zeros, hence 1112064 even zeros. Direct sums on 276 pairs and 10626 quartets gave zero and 864 zeros respectively. Adjacency-preserving enumeration found 48 automorphisms and the quartic zeros partitioned into fifteen size-48 and six size-24 orbits. The empty frequency gives 600, hence the condition number is 150 and the pseudoinverse norm is 1/4. Averaging any range projection over translations gives the unique range projection diagonal in Walsh coordinates, without increasing either endpoint norm. The inverse-transform kernel is supported on the linear parity subspace and its absolute sum was 117884/8192 = 29471/2048.
residual_risks: The computation is a finite census on L(Q3), not an all-graphs formula.

evidence: The orientation count is a coefficient of the edge product ∏(t_u+t_v); replacing a plus with a signed term on a selected edge gives its signed analogue. The planar degree-four count also has the dual proper 3-coloring formulation, divided by three: an edge step modulo three is ±1 and the even divergence at a degree-four vertex must be zero if divisible by three.
The exact local match is the same frozen record. The distinct C7² analogue has a 14-coordinate spectrum and starts its nontrivial even cancellations at weight two.

value.rationale: The cuboctahedron is a natural finite four-regular ice graph. The finding distinguishes reversal-forbidden frequencies from extra even blind modes, classifies the lowest such modes, and gives exact rank and conditioning data. The projection constant controls the best endpoint norm even for projections not designed by Fourier symmetry. These motivated invariants are useful for comparison with other graph-ice recovery models and are not given merely by a state count.
residual_risks: No uniform behavior across larger or different graphs follows.
